assets.prompt: Use case: game UI skin asset. Generate ONE isolated EMPTY reusable rectangular panel skin for raylib nine-slice rendering, on a genuinely transparent RGBA background. The attached image is the APPROVED STYLE REFERENCE: reproduce its thin blue-gray steel stepped panel frame and warm ivory enamel interior very faithfully. This is the empty outer panel/card frame, NOT a screenshot. Front-facing flat pixel art, horizontal rectangle with aspect approximately 3:2, occupying about 85% of canvas with transparent margin around all sides. A continuous slim layered stepped steel border, dark forest-green inner outline, simple light blue-gray highlight on top/left and darker blue-gray shadow below/right. Exactly four small copper screw heads, one tucked in each corner, matching reference. Large fully opaque blank light warm ivory center, essentially uniform color for dynamic text and controls. No header bands, no interior dividers, no slots, no text, no letters, no numbers, no symbols, no icons, no leaves, no wood, no extra UI pieces, no scene, no mockup, no perspective, no realistic metal texture, no rust, no gradient background, no shadows outside the small pixel frame edge. Clean crisp low-resolution-style pixel edges and limited palette; maintain the same modest industrial skin as the reference menu, not elaborate machinery. The straight edge middle sections and blank center must be suitable for stretching independently while preserving four corners. Only this one complete panel, all corners visible, with real transparency outside and opaque ivory center.

Use case: game UI skin asset. Generate ONE isolated EMPTY reusable horizontal button / tab skin, on a genuinely transparent RGBA background. Attached image is the approved style reference. Precisely match the small stepped steel-frame buttons 'Voltar' and the top stage tabs of that reference, with steel blue-gray layered border and blank warm ivory enamel center. Long horizontal rectangular shape about 5:1, with small stepped clipped corners, slim dark green inner outline, modest gray-blue highlight on upper edge and darker lower edge. Flat front-facing crisp pixel art, limited palette. Center is opaque and completely blank; border is thin and suitable for nine-slice resizing. No screws needed on this small button, no decorative icons, no letters, no numbers, NO TEXT, no cursor, no arrows, no separate parts, no scene, no wood, no leaves, no rust, no machinery, no realistic textures, no cast shadow or glow beyond the edge. The ENTIRE AREA OUTSIDE the one button must have alpha ZERO; do not draw any colored background, vignette, checkerboard pattern or haze. Leave transparent padding around all four sides and do not crop the button. One complete button only. Selection and amber focus will be drawn dynamically in game.

Use case: pixel-art game control sprite. Generate ONE isolated relay rocker switch WITH its tiny state lamp immediately to its right, exactly matching the ON control from the attached approved menu style reference. This is just a small reusable control sprite, NOT a card, NOT a menu. Genuine transparent RGBA background, alpha zero everywhere outside the control. The assembly is centered with ample transparent padding. The rocker is a simple tall vertical rectangle in a slim dark charcoal stepped housing with two steel-gray pixel bevel bands. Its UPPER half is bright leaf green, indicating ON; lower half medium gray. A tiny green circular/octagonal pixel indicator lamp sits to the right at the rocker's vertical center, with a dark outline, lime body and one tiny pale highlight. Preserve the modest simple pixel-art proportions of the reference: rocker about 2.3 times as tall as wide, lamp about half the rocker width, gap about half rocker width. Crisp big intentional pixel clusters and short stepped corners, flat front-facing view, dark outlines, no perspective, no realistic material rendering. Only one switch and one lamp in a single complete sprite; no extra components, wires, panel frame, card background, buttons, labels, numbers, text, arrows, wood, leaves, glow or cast shadow. All outside pixels must be truly transparent, not black, white, checkered or vignetted. This is the ON state of a pair, designed to be redrawn later in the same pose and dimensions as the OFF state.

Edit target: image 1, the isolated relay switch and lamp. Supporting style reference: image 2. Produce its matching OFF state. Keep EXACTLY the same canvas dimensions, control position, housing silhouette, pixel scale, rocker size, lamp center and margins as image 1. Change ONLY the states: upper half of rocker becomes medium gray; lower half becomes muted brick red, indicating OFF. The small lamp to the right changes from green to muted brick red with a small pale highlight. Preserve the front-facing crisp simple pixel art and dark charcoal / blue-gray steel outlines. IMPORTANT: remove all luminous haze and cast shadows around the control, leave the entire exterior and gap between housing and lamp genuinely transparent with alpha zero. The object itself stays opaque. No text, labels, panel frame, extra sprites, shadows, gradients, checkered pattern or colored background. This is one complete isolated OFF control asset for a game, and must match the ON reference's object registration precisely.
